subject: maths
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

covers: Count objects up to 20 using pictures, things and written numerals
Say and write numbers from 1 to 20, and recognise numbers up to 99
Group objects by shape, size or other visible features
Compare numbers up to 20 and put them in order
Make two-digit numbers from given digit cards
Find the numbers before, after and between two others
Bundle sticks into tens and ones to see what each digit means
Understand zero as what is left when everything is taken away
Use addition and subtraction of numbers up to 20 in everyday life
Build addition facts up to 9 with objects
Subtract within 9 by taking away
Tell short number stories that match an addition or subtraction
Add and subtract numbers up to 99 without carrying or borrowing
Solve everyday problems shown in pictures or told in words
Describe the features of solid shapes in their own words
Name and recognise cuboid, cylinder, cone and sphere
Trace the outline of a 3D object to get a 2D shape
Name rectangle, square, triangle and circle
Tell straight lines from curved lines
Draw straight lines that are vertical, horizontal or slanting
Link shapes to objects around them
Measure short lengths with body units such as a finger or hand span
Estimate a length, then check it by measuring
Use words like near, far, longer, taller and shorter to compare
Compare how heavy or light objects are
Order containers from smallest to largest capacity
Put events in order of time, such as earlier and later
Tell apart events that take a short time from those that take a long time
Collect simple information from daily life, such as birthdays or favourites
Record what they collect with pictures or numerals
Read and explain information shown in simple visuals
Notice patterns in shapes and numbers around them
Extend and complete a sequence
Explain why a pattern should continue the way it does

gaps: Teaching processes and learning resources are left out; the file lists only what a child learns.
